hero.title: Gojek × Navier — the super-app, on the water of the world's largest archipelago
hero.subtitle: Indonesia is 17,000+ islands and Gojek is its home-grown super-app. Water is the transport surface no one owns yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Gojek-branded foiling water tier across Indonesia's densest island crossings and cross-border corridors — booked in-app, premium-priced, category-defining in the largest archipelago on earth. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the network playbook now proven in the Maldives; Gojek brings the demand, the app, GoPay, and home-turf reach across Indonesia and Singapore. Together we turn slow, weather-exposed, accident-prone ferry crossings into fast, smooth, safe in-app water trips — and claim the category in the one country where water is the nation.

partner_context.their_ambition: You are Indonesia's home-grown super-app — Gojek, the mobility and payments core of GoTo, the largest digital ecosystem in the world's fourth-most-populous nation. Mobility is your founding business, and after sharpening focus (exiting Vietnam in 2024 and Thailand in 2021) your 2026 playbook is to deepen and defend your two markets — your vast Indonesian home and your strategic Singapore showcase — and drive them to durable profitability.
partner_context.their_pressure: Ride-hail on land in your home market is maturing and fiercely contested with Grab. Your next leg of high-margin growth comes from new surfaces, not from squeezing the road — and you operate across the largest archipelago on earth, where 17,000+ islands and the busiest international ferry corridors run on slow, ageing, accident-prone diesel boats that no super-app has ever monetized.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Water is the transport surface of Indonesia itself — and no super-app owns it. Navier turns it into a tier in your app: a software-defined foiling fleet, booked in Gojek, premium-priced, on the densest island crossings and cross-border corridors in the archipelago you call home — the same network model already ramping at scale in the Maldives.

partner_json_extract.why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging-infrastructure dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026), Singapore's regulator is mandating clean harbour craft from 2030, and Indonesia's most-trafficked crossings (Bali↔Nusa, Batam↔Singapore) are infamous for slow, accident-prone diesel boats. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster — and the world's largest archipelago is the surface that matters most.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged in Gojek's own backyard: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out); a ~100-vessel network is ramping in the Maldives; and Indonesia's busiest, most safety-troubled crossings — Bali↔Nusa, Batam↔Singapore — are ready to be switched onto a clean foiling tier in the app Indonesians already live in.

network_thesis.headline: One app. The world's largest archipelago. The water layer of Indonesia's super-app.
network_thesis.body: Indonesia is 17,000+ islands across 5,000 km of ocean — the most water-defined nation on earth — and Gojek is its home-grown super-app, operating across the archipelago and in Singapore. The same in-app foiling tier proven in the Maldives extends to every island crossing and cross-border corridor Gojek serves: pick one market to prove it, or roll the recommended sequence below. The fleet, the app integration, and the captain-partner model are identical everywhere.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Each card is a real, ready market. Start with Jakarta — Gojek's founding city and cleanest first proof point — or pick any cluster. The phased sequence below is our recommended path, not the only one.
network_thesis.coverage_note: Gojek is Indonesia's home-grown super-app across the world's largest archipelago, plus its strategic Singapore market; these six are where the water demand is densest and most visible today. The same fleet and in-app tier extend to every island crossing and cross-border corridor Gojek already serves.

partner_json_extract.multimodal_fit: Gojek already runs the hardest parts: real-time demand, dispatch, dynamic pricing, GoPay, and a GoRide/GoCar driver-partner network across Indonesia and Singapore. A foiling water tier slots straight in — same app, same wallet, captain-partners instead of driver-partners, the water leg booked door-to-door with the GoRide to and from the pier. Navier is simply the missing surface in a multimodal map Gojek already operates across the archipelago.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined and autonomy-ready — the same software-first instincts you bring. A factory in Turkey for supply, and a ~100-vessel at-scale network already proving the model in the Maldives — directly relevant to an archipelago of 17,000+ islands.

proof_points.claim: Mobility and on-demand is GoTo's largest revenue engine.
proof_points.evidence: On-demand services (Gojek's mobility + delivery) generated IDR 12.36 trillion in FY2025 — ~67.5% of GoTo's IDR 18.3T revenue (+24% YoY). A premium in-app water tier compounds the segment that already carries the company.

proof_points.claim: The super-app the water tier plugs into is now at scale and turning profitable.
proof_points.evidence: GoTo posted IDR 124 trillion of group GTV in 2025 with core GTV up 49% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of ~IDR 2T (ahead of guidance), then delivered its first-ever quarterly net profit in Q1 2026.

proof_points.claim: Indonesia's regulators are pulling marine toward clean fleets.
proof_points.evidence: Indonesia's Ministry of Transportation prioritises maritime decarbonisation toward a net-zero-by-2060 goal, with a national electric-boat program piloted in Jakarta's Thousand Islands; on the cross-border side, Singapore mandates fully electric / net-zero-fuel new harbour craft from 2030.
proof_points.source: ICCT / Kemenhub 2025; Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore

proof_points.claim: The cross-border demand already exists — on diesel boats.
proof_points.evidence: Batam's ferry terminals alone served ~4.2 million passengers in the first half of 2024 (+6% YoY), the bulk of it crossing to and from Singapore on one of the world's busiest international ferry corridors — both Gojek markets.

objections.concern: Is the range enough across an archipelago?
objections.response: The dense everyday crossings — Jakarta's Thousand Islands (~12 nm), Bali↔Nusa (~12 nm), Singapore↔Batam/Bintan (~12-22 nm), Labuan Bajo↔Komodo (~18 nm) — all sit well inside the Pioneer II 70 nm all-electric envelope. The long eastern frontier legs (Sangihe-Talaud, Raja Ampat outliers, Flores) run on the Quanta-LR hybrid at 700 nm range, with no charging infrastructure required anywhere.

objections.concern: Indonesian crossings have a serious safety reputation problem.
objections.response: That is exactly the opening. The 2025 Bali Strait ferry sinking is the kind of event that makes the status quo untenable. Foils lift the hull clear of the surface so the ride is smooth where displacement boats pound; software-defined controls, a clear first-of-class certification path, and an operating record across the US and the Maldives make a Navier tier the safe, premium alternative travellers will actively choose.

objections.concern: Can this be profitable, not just a flagship?
objections.response: On-demand is already GoTo's biggest revenue engine; a foiling tier monetises premium crossings users take today on unmonetised diesel ferries, at a price point the affluent leisure and cross-border flows support. It rides the same app, wallet, dispatch and pricing rails Gojek already runs — captain-partners instead of driver-partners — so the marginal cost of adding the surface is low.

Sheltered-strait routing plus the Quanta-LR's range give the network the flexibility to keep running and reposition through monsoon windows, and the foiling ride is more weather-tolerant than the ferries it replaces — that reliability is the premium.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR hybrid), the network and operations playbook proven at scale in the Maldives, captain-partner training, and the first-of-class certification path for Indonesian and Singaporean waters.
the_ask.partner_brings: You bring demand and dispatch through the Gojek app, GoPay, the brand, the captain-partner model, and the home-turf regulatory relationships across Indonesia and Singapore.
the_ask.next_step: A Bali or Jakarta pilot MOU: co-define the in-app foiling water tier on three corridors, then scale across the archipelago cluster by cluster.

close.title: One app. 17,000 islands. The water layer of Indonesia's super-app.
close.body: Bali proves it, Jakarta Bay turns it into daily mobility, the Singapore crossing makes it cross-border, and Komodo, Sulawesi and Raja Ampat carry it east across the frontier. From there the same playbook extends across every island crossing Gojek already serves — the water layer of the world's largest archipelago, booked entirely inside the super-app.

markets_or_footprint.label: Jakarta
markets_or_footprint.summary: Jakarta is Gojek's birthplace and the densest demand pool in the company's home market — a ~10M-person megacity (greater Jabodetabek ~32M) ringed by Jakarta Bay and the Thousand Islands (Kepulauan Seribu), and ranked among the most congestion-choked cities on earth. The bay and islands are served today by slow, weather-exposed wooden ferries from Marina Ancol and Muara Angke. This is the water layer of Gojek's home city: an in-app foiling tier that turns Jakarta Bay into a commuter and leisure h…

markets_or_footprint.label: Bali, Nusa & the Gili Islands
markets_or_footprint.summary: Bali is Indonesia's tourism engine and one of Gojek's densest leisure-demand markets — and the crossings around it are notoriously bad. The Bali↔Nusa Penida/Lembongan and Bali↔Gili Islands fast-boat routes are among the most-trafficked and most safety-troubled tourist water corridors in Southeast Asia, run by a fragmented fleet of overloaded diesel speedboats with a poor reliability and incident record. This is the highest-visibility water-mobility fix in Indonesia: an in-app foiling tier that r…

markets_or_footprint.label: Komodo & Flores
markets_or_footprint.summary: Labuan Bajo, the gateway to Komodo National Park, is Indonesia's fastest-rising marquee destination — a government 'super-priority' tourism zone with a new international airport and a booming liveaboard and day-boat market. Today the Komodo park, the pink-sand beaches, Padar and the surrounding Flores arc are served almost entirely by slow diesel cruise boats and phinisi schooners. This is a premium island-hopping market tailor-made for a clean foiling tier: an in-app Gojek water layer that turn…

markets_or_footprint.label: Riau Islands ↔ Singapore
markets_or_footprint.summary: The Batam/Bintan↔Singapore corridor is one of the busiest international ferry crossings on earth — millions of cross-border trips a year between Singapore's harbour and the Riau Islands resorts and industrial zones, run today on a fleet of ageing diesel fast-ferries. This is the one corridor where Gojek operates on BOTH ends: its Indonesian home market on the Riau side and its only overseas market in Singapore. A clean foiling tier here is uniquely powerful — a cross-border, in-app water connect…

markets_or_footprint.label: Singapore
markets_or_footprint.summary: Singapore is Gojek's only market outside Indonesia — a dense, affluent, water-ringed city-state whose harbour, Southern Islands and Sentosa waterfront are under-used for mobility, and whose regulator is mandating clean harbour craft from 2030. This is Gojek's overseas proof point: a clean foiling water tier in a world-class maritime city, bookable in the same app, that showcases the model to international partners and connects directly to the cross-border Riau corridor.

markets_or_footprint.label: Eastern Indonesia Frontier
markets_or_footprint.summary: Eastern Indonesia — North Sulawesi (Manado/Bunaken/Likupang), Wakatobi, Raja Ampat in West Papua — is the country's diving and marine-tourism frontier: world-class seascapes spread across vast open water, served today only by liveaboards, infrequent flights and slow boats. As Gojek deepens its national super-app reach, this is the long-range frontier where Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range turns scattered, hard-to-reach islands into a connected in-app network — a clean foiling layer across the pla…
